proof_dependencies.accepted_scope: Extends a proper filter with a verified finite-intersection generating family; available in ZFC. Used separately for fixed-record existence and coupling constructions.

Orbit representative selection, choosing a point from every nonempty coordinate fixed set, and extracting countably infinite subsets of arbitrary infinite sets. All are allowed by the stated ZFC hypothesis.

proof_dependencies.dependency: Stone representation and Boolean quotient correspondence
proof_dependencies.accepted_scope: Elementary inverse-image correspondence and basic clopens are proved in the reference. Compact Hausdorff zero-dimensional facts follow from the closed realization in a product of finite discrete spaces, using ZFC compactness.
Finite G-set counts apply to arbitrary groups acting on a finite set; no finiteness of G is introduced.

independent_proof_audit.claim: Empty sets and the first layer
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: For X empty, Map(X,[0]) is singleton and r_0 would be a function singleton→empty, impossible. For nonempty X, Map(X,[0]) is empty and r_0 is unique. The [1] layer is unique, and maps [1]→[n] force all constants.
assumptions: all groups, sets and index families are sets

independent_proof_audit.claim: All binary records are exactly independent complement-pair orientations
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: Constants fix c(empty)=0,c(X)=1; the binary transposition gives c(A complement)=1-c(A). Every map among [0],[1],[2] is vacuous, constant, identity or transposition, so the converse has no missing naturality constraints. No intersection closure is implicitly imposed.
assumptions: all groups, sets and index families are sets

independent_proof_audit.claim: Stabilization at three and all higher tests
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: Each ordered three-block partition, including empty blocks, has exactly one chosen block by all three singleton characteristic maps [3]→[2]. This implies integer-valued disjoint additivity, hence upward and intersection closure, yielding a proper ultrafilter. Conversely a proper ultrafilter chooses one finite fibre and upward closure proves all-map naturality. The proof never imports an unavailable four-valued test at m=3.
assumptions: all groups, sets and index families are sets

independent_proof_audit.claim: All ordinary restriction images and fibres and functoriality
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: Under the classifications, high-to-high maps are identities, high-to-binary maps have a singleton fibre precisely at ultrafilter orientations, all other binary target fibres are empty, and restrictions to layer one have the entire source as their sole fibre. Same-layer identities and empty-to-empty maps are covered. Set-map actions are inverse-image of subsets/pushforward of ultrafilters, so composition and every restriction commute.
assumptions: all groups, sets and index families are sets

independent_proof_audit.claim: Finite G-set fixed records and every restricted fixed fibre
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: A binary orientation can be transported across a complement-pair orbit iff no stabilizer swaps the two sides, equivalently no g,A satisfy gA=X\A. Each orbit then contributes exactly two choices, independently. High records are principal because X is finite, and fixedness means the point belongs to X^G. Therefore high-to-binary fixed maps have singleton fibres at the fixed principal orientations and empty fibres otherwise; fixed maps to layer one have entire source fibre, possibly empty.
assumptions: all groups, sets and index families are sets

independent_proof_audit.claim: Observation topology and intrinsic Boolean model
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: Every finite observation fibre is the clopen membership set of one subset of X; binary observations already generate all such sets. The Boolean ideal of sets disjoint from some X^H is downward and finite-union closed because finitely many finite generating sets generate a finitely generated subgroup. Avoiding the ideal is equivalent to containing every X^H. Boolean quotient ultrafilters pull back bijectively, with identical membership clopens. The improper ideal correctly gives an empty Stone space.
assumptions: all groups, sets and index families are sets

independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: For one permutation g, every moved orbit is an even cycle, an odd cycle, or a bi-infinite integer orbit. Choice of orbit representatives permits a proper coloring with three colors so each color C is disjoint from gC. An invariant ultrafilter concentrating on the moved set would contain one color and its disjoint translate, a contradiction. Hence it contains Fix(g). Conversely A and g^{-1}A agree on Fix(g), so containing Fix(g) implies g-invariance. This proves the criterion for every individual g without a finite-generation hypothesis.
assumptions: choice of representatives for all permutation orbits

independent_proof_audit.claim: Nonemptiness iff every finitely generated subgroup has a fixed point
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: Invariant ultrafilters contain finite intersections of Fix(g), exactly X^H for finitely generated H. Conversely these sets have the finite-intersection property because a finite union of finite generating sets is finite. Extending the generated proper filter produces an invariant ultrafilter. H=1 is included, so empty X does not become a false positive.
assumptions: ultrafilter extension for a proper filter

independent_proof_audit.claim: Closure of actual fixed points and the exact criterion for one action
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: The closure of principal points from F=X^G is exactly all ultrafilters containing F. If no finite S satisfies X^{<S>}=F, then X^{<S>}\F is nonempty for every finite S, so all Fix(g) together with X\F have the finite-intersection property. Extension gives an invariant ultrafilter outside that closure. The converse follows from finite intersection membership. The proof handles empty F, empty X and empty S.
assumptions: all groups, sets and index families are sets

independent_proof_audit.claim: Universal group criterion is exactly finite generation
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: Finite generators make X^G a finite intersection of element-fixed sets for every action. If G is not finitely generated, form the set-indexed disjoint union of G/H over all finitely generated H. Every H is proper, so every orbit has no G-fixed point. Each finitely generated K fixes the coset K in its own branch. Thus the complete fixed-record space is nonempty while actual-fixed-point closure is empty. No countability or normality of H is assumed.
assumptions: all groups, sets and index families are sets

independent_proof_audit.claim: Countable concrete action and its entire fixed space
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: FSym(N) is a countable union of finite permutation groups indexed by the countable finite subsets of N. No natural number is fixed by every transposition. Each individual permutation fixes a cofinite set, so every nonprincipal ultrafilter is invariant. A principal invariant ultrafilter would be an actual fixed point, hence none exists. Therefore the full fixed space is exactly all nonprincipal ultrafilters, with the beta(N) minus N subspace topology.
assumptions: all groups, sets and index families are sets

independent_proof_audit.claim: Arbitrary-index product surjectivity, continuity and empty cases
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: Equivariant projections yield fixed marginal ultrafilters and continuity follows by composing finite observations. Given every marginal U_i, impose both all U_i cylinder sets and every product fixed set P^H. For finitely many constraints, combine the subgroup constraints into one finitely generated H; U_i contains X_i^H, hence all finitely constrained intersections are nonempty. Choice supplies points in all coordinates. Extending this proper filter gives an invariant coupling with precisely the prescribed margins. Empty index gives singleton→singleton. Empty RHS forces empty LHS via the projections; an empty underlying factor is included.

independent_proof_audit.claim: Every finite factor yields a bijection for arbitrary actions
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: A fixed ultrafilter on a nonempty finite factor is a principal ultrafilter at an actual fixed point x. Any coupling with that margin contains the slice {x}×Y, so the second margin uniquely determines it as the pushforward along y↦(x,y). This map is equivariant because x is fixed. Empty fixed spaces and empty factors give empty→empty, which is a bijection.
assumptions: all groups, sets and index families are sets

independent_proof_audit.claim: Optimal trivial-group injectivity criterion and failure with no actual fixed points
independent_proof_audit.independent_argument_checked: When both X,Y are infinite, ZFC gives injections of N and a free ultrafilter. The diagonal pushforward and a filter extension containing the complement of that diagonal have the same two margins. Every required rectangle meets the complement because both index preimages are infinite and two different indices can be chosen. They are distinct, proving necessity of a finite factor. For FSym(N), any coupling with free margins contains Fix(g)×Fix(g) for each g, hence is genuinely invariant; the diagonal/off-diagonal pair therefore disproves injectivity even when both original fixed sets are empty.
assumptions: all groups, sets and index families are sets

restriction_fibre_audit.ordinary_empty_X: All source/target record sets empty; each restriction is the unique empty bijection, with no target fibres.
ordinary_nonempty_X: Same-level restrictions are identities, every fibre singleton.
For m>=k>=3, under the ultrafilter models the restriction is identity; every fibre singleton.
For m>=3,k=2, image is exactly the ultrafilter orientations; each such target has one lift, every other target has no lift.
For k=1, the unique target has the whole source as fibre: singleton at m=1, all orientations at m=2, all ultrafilters at m>=3.
finite_fixed_X: Empty X again gives empty maps.
Nonempty X: first fixed layer is singleton; binary fixed layer has size 0 if a complement swap exists, otherwise 2^d for d complement-pair orbits; each high fixed layer is X^G.
High-to-high fixed restrictions are identities on X^G.
High-to-binary fixed target fibres are singleton at fixed principal orientations and empty at every other fixed orientation.
Every fixed restriction to layer one has the entire fixed source as its sole fibre, which may be empty; no unsupported surjectivity is inferred.

finite factor with no invariant records

findings.title: Do not require unrequested topological corollaries for full credit
findings.evidence: Task target 2 asks for a topology-compatible intrinsic classification; it does not separately request compactness, Hausdorffness, zero-dimensionality or density of all original point records. Check A1 currently lists all four as mandatory full-credit achievements.
findings.impact: A correct complete alternative classification and topology comparison could lose points for omitting unrequested side results. The listed consequences are mathematically correct, so this is a grading-contract defect rather than an invalid reference theorem.
findings.requested_fix: Keep A1 focused on the observation topology and a homeomorphic intrinsic model, or state explicitly that these standard consequences are explanatory and never separate grounds for deduction.
findings.resolution: A1 now makes the extra topological consequences optional and forbids deductions for omitting them.

findings.title: Accept a complete extension classification without an extra example
findings.evidence: Task target 1 requests the exact extension range. Check T5 full additionally requires a finite sharpness example or a separate sharpness argument.
findings.impact: The stated necessary-and-sufficient extension criteria with full proof already solve the target; a further example is useful reference material but an unrequested deliverable.
findings.requested_fix: Remove the mandatory example requirement or explicitly say a fully proved exact extension classification receives full credit without an example.
findings.resolution: T5 now explicitly gives full credit for the complete extension classification without an extra example or sharpness demonstration.

T5.obligation: State the exact fixed-record extension range at every finite level and justify that the obstruction can occur.
T5.full: First-layer extension is equivalent to nonempty full fixed space, binary extension is equivalent to being a fixed ultrafilter orientation and is unique, and all higher layers extend uniquely; a verified finite example or equivalent sharpness argument exhibits the nonextension possibility.
T5.half: Correct extension criterion but no sharpness evidence, or gives a valid obstruction without the complete criterion.
T5.zero: Claims every finite-level fixed record extends, or gives neither valid criterion nor obstruction.

A1.obligation: Identify the observation topology with the Stone topology and justify its compact Hausdorff realization, point density and compatibility with the action.
A1.full: Finite-fibre inverse images are membership clopens, binary observations generate the topology, compact Hausdorff zero-dimensional realization and density are established, and group maps act by homeomorphisms.
A1.half: Correct basic clopens and continuity but a material topological property or density argument is omitted.
A1.zero: Uses a different topology without proving equality, or supplies no valid topological realization.
